chunks.text: PROCEDURE EMP-SOP-014 — EQUIPMENT INSPECTION AND APPROVAL (Rev 7) 1. PURPOSE This procedure defines how inspection findings are reviewed and how an equipment approval note is issued after a statutory or shutdown inspection at MRPL. 2. APPROVAL NOTE REQUIREMENTS An approval note for returned-to-service decisions MUST contain: a. Equipment tag and report number. b. A statement of each finding with severity (UNACCEPTABLE / ACCEPTABLE). c. Cross-reference to the applicable acceptance criteria in PV-MAN-02. d. Conditions imposed before restart (repairs, re-rating, monitoring). e. The inspector name, date, and the approving authority signature block. 3. SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION Any wall thickness below the minimum required thickness in PV-MAN-02 is classified UNACCEPTABLE and the equipment must not return to service until repaired or formally re-rated.

n PV-MAN-02 is classified UNACCEPTABLE and the equipment must not return to service until repaired or formally re-rated. Any hydro test pressure loss greater than 5 percent per hour is classified UNACCEPTABLE. 4. ESCALATION Findings classified UNACCEPTABLE are escalated to the Inspection Manager within 24 hours. Approval notes for UNACCEPTABLE findings require the counter-signature of the Inspection Manager. 5. RECORDS The signed approval note is filed with the inspection dossier and a copy is sent to the Mechanical Records Office.

STORAGE TANK OPERATIONS MANUAL OPS-MAN-07 (Rev 9) SECTION 3 — TEMPERATURE LIMITS 3.1 The maximum permitted product temperature in atmospheric storage tanks containing crude and middle distillates is 90 degrees Celsius at the tank bottom sensing point. 3.2 If the tank temperature exceeds 90 degrees Celsius, the operator must immediately start the tank cooling water spray, stop any circulation or heating medium flow, and inform the Shift In-charge. 3.3 Temperatures above 95 degrees Celsius for more than 15 minutes require a Level-2 incident report per HSE-MAN-11, and the tank must be isolated for inspection before it is returned to service. PRESSURE VESSEL INTEGRITY MANUAL PV-MAN-02 (Rev 4) SECTION 5 — MINIMUM THICKNESS AND CORROSION ALLOWANCE 5.1 The minimum required thickness of a pressure shell is the thickness required by the design code PLUS corrosion allowance for the intended service life. Operating below the minimum required thickness is prohibited. 5.2 For carbon steel shells in crude overhead service, the typical corrosion allowance is 3.0 mm and the design life basis is 20 years. Where measured thickness is below the minimum required thickness, the component must be re-rated, repaired or replaced. 5.3 Re-rating requires a fitness-for-service calculation by the Engineering Department and formal re-rating approval. SECTION 8 — HYDROSTATIC TESTING 8.1 Hydro test acceptance: pressure loss shall not exceed 5 percent per hour during the hold period. Any visible leakage is cause for immediate rejection of the test.

not exceed 5 percent per hour during the hold period. Any visible leakage is cause for immediate rejection of the test. 8.2 Leaking tubes may be plugged provided the plugged tube count does not exceed 10 percent of the total tube count per pass; otherwise retubing is required. My Responses : 1. Why do you want to be a part of this group ? * My interest in neuroscience comes from my interest in AI. The more I learn about neural networks, deep learning and intelligent systems, the more I realise that we are still trying to understand something that biology has already been doing incredibly well the brain. I want to understand the fundamentals of how the brain learns, remembers, perceives and makes decisions, and see what we can learn from it while building AI. More than just attending sessions, I would love to explore papers, discuss ideas and eventually work on small research projects with the group. 2. Would something like this be beneficial for your overall knowledge growth ? Briefly explain I've spent most of my time learning intelligence from the engineering side ; AI, machine learning, neural networks and robotics.

nt most of my time learning intelligence from the engineering side ; AI, machine learning, neural networks and robotics. But the more I learn about these systems, the more interesting the biological version becomes. The brain is the original learning system, and we still don't completely understand how it achieves what it does. I'd like to learn the neuroscience behind it rather than just taking inspiration from the brain at a very high level. I'm also looking for a group where I can discuss ideas, read papers, ask questions and eventually build things or experiment with them . I don't expect to understand computational neuroscience immediately. That's actually one of the reasons I want to join. 3.
